redirectUri.required: Enter at least one redirect URI.
redirectUri.whitespace: A redirect URI cannot contain spaces. Put each URI on its own line.
redirectUri.fragment: A redirect URI cannot contain a fragment (#…).
redirectUri.query: A redirect URI cannot contain a query string (?…); Free2Z appends its own.
redirectUri.notAbsolute: Use an absolute URI with a scheme, such as https://app.example.com/callback.
redirectUri.credentials: A redirect URI cannot contain a username or password.
redirectUri.localhost: “localhost” is not accepted because it may resolve off the device. Use http://127.0.0.1:<port>/… or http://[::1]:<port>/… (RFC 8252 §8.3).
redirectUri.httpNotLoopback: Plain http is accepted only for the loopback address (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/…). Use https everywhere else.
redirectUri.badPort: The loopback port is not valid.
redirectUri.loopbackNoPath: A loopback redirect needs a path, such as http://127.0.0.1:0/callback.
redirectUri.httpsNoHost: An https redirect needs a host.
redirectUri.httpsLoopback: Loopback redirects use http, not https (RFC 8252 §7.3).
redirectUri.badScheme: Use https, loopback http, or a reverse-DNS app scheme you control, such as com.example.app (RFC 8252 §7.1).
redirectUri.privateSchemeSlashes: An app scheme takes one slash after the colon: com.example.app:/oauth/callback.
redirectUri.privateSchemeNoPath: An app scheme redirect needs a path: com.example.app:/oauth/callback.
redirectUri.confidentialHttpsOnly: A server-side (confidential) app may only register https redirect URIs.
